title: A WARM WELCOME, A WATCHFUL EYE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "As soon as Laban heard the news about Jacob, his sister's son, he hurried to meet him. He embraced him and kissed him and brought him to his home, and there Jacob told him all these things. Then Laban said to him, 'You are my own flesh and blood.' After Jacob had stayed with him for a whole month, Laban said to him, 'Just because you are a relative of mine, should you work for me for nothing? Tell me what your wages should be.'" - Gen 29:13-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Laban greets Jacob warmly — embracing him, kissing him, welcoming him home as "my own flesh and blood." It is a heartfelt reception, and Jacob must have felt wonderfully received after his lonely journey. Yet within a month, a different side of Laban begins to show. He raises the question of wages — and as the chapter unfolds, we discover that Laban is a shrewd, self-serving man who will use Jacob for his own gain.

People are not always exactly as their first warm welcome suggests. This is not a call to cynicism or suspicion of everyone, but a reminder to walk with wisdom. Jesus told His followers to be "as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves" (Matt 10:16) — combining genuine kindness with clear-eyed discernment.

Jacob, who had used others through deception, was now going to spend years under a man who would use him. God was allowing Jacob to experience, from the other side, what it felt like to be dealt with unfairly.

In our own relationships, we can be warm and trusting while still being wise. Not everyone who smiles has our best interests at heart, and that is alright — our security rests not in people's reliability but in God's. Let us love people openly, yet lean our whole weight only on the Lord.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I combining kindness with wise discernment in my relationships?
2. Where do I need to lean on God rather than on people's promises?
3. Have I experienced being treated the way I once treated others?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me a heart that is warm and trusting, yet wise and discerning. Help me to love people openly while resting my security fully in You. Amen.
